audit_findings.title: Owner earnings mixes consolidated subsidiary cash flows with a parent-only share denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: OE uses parent-attributable net income but consolidated depreciation, working-capital movements and capital expenditures, while per-share value uses only Vail common shares; consolidated cash in the bridge may have the same perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.evidence: On August 3, 2022, through a wholly-owned subsidiary, the Company acquired a 55 % controlling interest in Andermatt-Sedrun from Andermatt Swiss Alps AG (“ASA”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated methodological error, not merely a possibility. Material outside ownership includes 45% of Andermatt-Sedrun, 25% of Whistler Blackcomb and approximately 16% of CMA. Filed 2025 net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $17.972 million, equal to 6.7% of the $268.3 million OE anchor, but that amount does not measure the omitted shares of depreciation, capital expenditure or working capital. The net effect can be positive or negative and is reasonably capable of altering the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year from cash-flow components attributable to Vail shareholders, reconcile the result to distributions and balances for noncontrolling interests, restrict bridge cash to Vail's distributable economic share, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Park City’s recurring landlord participation may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 cash payment $20.279 million, equal to 7.6% of anchor OE; April 2026 liability $93.0 million, or $2.53 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash fair-value expense may be added back to OE while the related cash participation payment remains in financing cash flow and is omitted; any economic obligation not represented by forecast payments would enter the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The lease for Park City provides for participating contingent payments (the “Contingent Consideration”) to the landlord of 42% of the amount by which EBITDA for the Park City resort operations, as calculated under the lease, exceeds inflation linked threshold and an adjustment equal to 10% of any capital improvements or investments made under the lease by the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring payment and liability are demonstrated by the filings, but their omission from OE is unresolved until the valuation adjustments are traced. The 2025 payment is large relative to the $268.3 million anchor and therefore capable of materially reducing operating value if omitted. The $93.0 million liability cannot automatically be deducted in addition to forecast participation payments because that could double count the same obligation.
audit_findings.action: Trace each year's fair-value charge, cash payment and OE adjustment; deduct recurring cash participation exactly once, identify any liability portion not represented in forecast OE, and rerun all scenarios with a documented no-double-count reconciliation.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may mistake seasonal operating cash for excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $371.374 million added to equity value, or $10.12 per diluted share and 9.0% of base equity value; April 2026 short-term deferred revenue was $467.041 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash as a nonoperating asset even though some may fund deferred pass obligations, seasonal losses, restricted subsidiary needs or minimum operating liquidity already reflected through working capital in OE
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred revenue balances of a short-term nature were $ 602.1 million and $ 575.8 million as of July 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: It is not demonstrated that all cash is unavailable, and deferred revenue is not a dollar-for-dollar cash restriction. Nevertheless, the entire $371.374 million balance was added without an excess-cash analysis, and its $10.12-per-share scale is material relative to the valuation. The possibility is therefore reasonably capable of changing value materially.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an April 2026 cash-availability schedule by legal entity that reconciles deferred revenue, restricted cash, expected seasonal cash burn, covenant liquidity and working-capital treatment; rerun the bridge using only parent-distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: EPR holds a property-purchase and leaseback right not captured by ordinary debt treatment
audit_findings.mechanism: Exercise would change the operating perimeter by transferring resort assets and would reduce future OE through lease rent not represented by current interest expense or historical lease costs
audit_findings.evidence: The EPR Agreements grant EPR certain other rights including the option to purchase the Boston Mills, Brandywine, Jack Frost, Big Boulder or Alpine Valley resorts, which is exercisable no sooner than two years and no later than one year prior to the maturity dates of the applicable EPR Secured Note for such properties, with any closings to be held on the applicable maturity dates; and, if EPR exercises the purchase option, EPR will enter into an agreement with the Company for the lease of each acquired property for an initial term of 20 years, plus options to extend the lease for two additional periods of ten years each.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual option is demonstrated, but no exercise, option price or future rent is established in the supplied record. Its exercise window is tied to the 2034 maturities, so this is a forward-looking exposure rather than a present valuation adjustment that can be measured now.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the EPR agreements' option-price and lease formulas and monitor exercise indications; before the exercise window, model the asset transfer and rent or an equivalent present-value claim.

audit_findings.title: A near-term concession outcome conflicts with the null perimeter ruling
audit_findings.mechanism: The concession outcome affects the forecast perimeter, GTLC operating earnings, concession fees and required capital expenditures included in perpetual OE and growth
audit_findings.evidence: The NPS has released a contract solicitation for the services offered by GTLC, and we intend to timely submit a bid on behalf of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 filing establishes that the existing GTLC arrangement was expected to extend only through December 2026 while a competitive solicitation was pending. The supplied record does not establish the concession's actual status as of the September 6, 2026 valuation date or disclose standalone GTLC cash economics. Loss or worse terms would reduce value, while favorable terms could increase it; materiality cannot be established from the available numbers.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the NPS award, extension or bid status effective September 6, 2026 and GTLC's attributable OE and maintenance capital; rerun the forecast using the awarded term and economics or remove GTLC after expiration.

audit_findings.title: The uncertain-tax claim is omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $56.8 million booked at July 31, 2025, or $1.55 per diluted share and 1.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement cash outflow not already borne by forecast taxes or OE would be deducted as a one-time claim in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Our reserves for uncertain tax positions, including any income tax related interest and penalties, are $56.8 million as of July 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, although whether it is an incremental economic omission depends on whether forecast tax expense already captures the claim. Even deducting the full filed reserve would reduce base value from $112.78 to approximately $111.23 per share and the 30%-MOS buy-below level from $78.95 to approximately $77.87; it would not change the conclusion relative to the $134.96 market price. The filing also anticipated a fiscal-2026 reduction from statutes of limitation.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the reserve outstanding at April 30, 2026 and reconcile it to forecast tax expense; if not already captured, deduct the non-duplicative booked amount from the bridge, without requiring a change to the materiality conclusion unless the updated exposure is substantially larger.
